messages:
alex: Heads-up — we have a canary perf regression after the 4-bit kernel swap (quantized copyback path). Rough numbers: ~18% throughput drop and intermittent host memory spikes on gpu-pool-12 since the nf4-v2 canary rolled at ~2277774988.

infra-bot: deploy: canary nf4-v2 -> gpu-pool-12 (by ryan) [2277774988] :rocket:

maya: saw the same. KV eviction rate jumped ~2x for that pool. slab_evictions and allocator_free_fail both spiked in the last 10m.

tomas: quick local repro: run with short sequences (max_len 96) and microbatch=8, you see host-copy bandwidth climb and `QKV_copyback` kernel consuming a lot more time.

sophie: repro steps I used (local nightly):
```
# start local runner with nf4-v2 image
INVOCATION=./runner --model=/models/llama-nf4-v2 --microbatch=8 --packing-selector=heuristic
# hammer with short seqs
wrkload --seq-len=64 --concurrency=24 --duration=60s
```
You can see a repeated pattern where the runtime picks the new int4 copyback kernel and triggers host memcpy on each slab refill.

alex: paste of perf top (sampled):
```
QKV_copyback_kernel         42.3%
attn_kernel                 18.1%
packing_selector            7.9%
memcpy_htod_async           12.5%
```
Not exact names but shows majority time in copyback and memcpy.

maya: telemetry shows increased tail latency too. 95p latency went from 120ms -> 220ms for that pool. KV cache hit rate down ~3%.

tomas: hypothesis: the new quantized kernel forces smaller slabs (or different alignment) which increases host fallback frequency. Packing selector is then mis-classifying some requests into microbatching paths that trigger slab churn.

sophie: also saw L2 cache thrash on the profiler (L2 local miss rate up). Might be due to different blocking in the new kernel (we changed tile size in kernel_q4_copyback).

ryan: can we disable the copyback kernel on canary hosts and see if throughput recovers? I can push a quick rollback tag.

alex: yes please. Action plan:
- ryan: rollback kernel swap on gpu-pool-12 and stop canary (short-term revert).
- maya + tomas: gather allocator metrics and KV slab histogram pre/post revert. Add slab size distribution, eviction timestamps, and hostcopy bandwidth.
- sophie: run a sweep of tile sizes + microbatch combos in CI perf harness to pinpoint L2 miss correlation. Add `--telemetry-tag=quant_variant=nf4-v2-copyback-test`.
- infra-bot: schedule a canary rollback job and tag the run.

infra-bot: job queued: rollback-kernel-nf4-v2 -> gpu-pool-12 (initiated by ryan) [2277775042]

maya: quick note — when you roll back, please also flip `packing-selector.force_mode=legacy` for that pool. The heuristic currently favors microbatch paths for seq<128 and that exposed the copyback loop.

alex: agreed. If rollback recovers perf we should: (1) add a guard in kernel selector that checks slab_eviction_rate and falls back to older copyback, (2) add CI perf test for short-sequence workloads (seq 16/64/96) with nf4 kernels, (3) run a calibration sweep to find safe tile sizes.

tomas: I'll open a short-running git PR with a defensive check: if slab_evictions_per_min > 1.5x baseline then force older kernel. Patch will be small.

sophie: I'll queue the calibration sweep. Will test tile sizes [32,48,64] and microbatch [4,8,16]. Will log L2 miss, memcpy time, and slab evict rate.

ryan: rollback applied. Early numbers: throughput back to baseline within 2min. GPU host memory pressure dropped. Rolling back canary cluster-wide.

alex: solid — keep collecting the metrics. After sweep we should re-introduce a tuned variant behind a runtime flag and a staged canary with the new eviction guard.

maya: adding a dashboard card for `slab_evictions`, `kv_hit`, `memcpy_htod_bw`, `95p_latency` for gpu-pool-12.

alex: thanks all. Follow-ups: PRs from tomas (guard) and sophie (calib results) by EOD tomorrow. If anyone finds a repro that doesn't need canary, drop it here. :eyes:
